correctness.rationale: The exact claim covers every k>=0 at n=3·4^k, distinct linear Thue–Morse factors, and palindrome pairs with an empty part allowed. For φ=μ² with palindromic blocks B0=0110, B1=1001, every cyclic φ-image has a reversal-invariant six-factor histogram because each six-factor uses at most three source letters and cyclic binary 3-grams obey reversal balance. A factor of length 4m with a seam between unequal boundary source letters acquires one of six exceptional four-blocks. Exhaustive local cases for six-factor reversal imbalance (six anomalous blocks × 16 nearby binary contexts, plus short circular cases) give a strictly positive obstruction, so such a word cannot be a palindrome pair. Equal-boundary factors are rotations of a φ-image; unique cyclic block decoding and reflection symmetry descend the palindrome-pair property. Base length three has exactly two rotation classes (010 and 101), and actual squares in Thue–Morse ensure every rotation survives at each induction step. Primitivity and disjointness descend as well, yielding exactly 2n. Independent local checks reproduced positive seam asymmetry minima and all-good symmetry; inspected separate factor-counter independently corroborates k=0..3 only, not the infinite proof.
